summary: The literature account is careful and honest. It cites the published question (Kulaichev 1984), the later work by Huet, Rao, Pustynski and Chiodo, and the search for prior formalizations, and it does not claim to answer Kulaichev's question. The paper-worthiness of this result group, taken alone, has not been shown. The fourth condition (the golden slope product) comes only from the submitter's own unreviewed preprints, through a construction with solids. No outside source asks for it. The account itself says it is one of several possible choices and cannot single out the yantra. The one feature that could interest a specialist audience, that the figure has the traditional 43 triangles and 24 sandhis, is certified outside Lean and is not part of the compared statements.

findings.message: The research interest of this result group, taken alone, has not been shown. The theorem proves uniqueness under a fourth condition, uv = 2/φ³, that the submitter introduced. Its only motivation is a construction with solids in the submitter's own unreviewed preprints (#29, #44, #103), and no published question or outside source asks for it. The account states that this condition and Kulaichev's congruence are 'two choices of that fourth condition', that the family 'cannot single out "the" yantra by itself', and that other conditions from solids (#103, Table 3) also give 43 triangles. Kulaichev's open question concerns his condition (a), which this entry replaces. The feature that might make this particular figure matter to researchers on Śrī Yantra geometry (Huet, Rao, Chiodo) is that it reproduces the traditional 43 triangles and 24 sandhis. That feature is outside the compared statements and outside Lean. What is formally compared is uniqueness for one choice among several, a choice the author made. To meet the requirement, the entry needs a reason a specialist would care about this condition: an outside source or published question that motivates it, or a compared statement that includes the property that makes the figure distinctive, such as the traditional region counts. Alternatively, the result could be presented together with the answer to Kulaichev's own question, which this candidate leaves out.

internal_notes.message: The proposed configuration names only the two theorems and the axioms. The definitions are listed here in the order of the Challenge file, because the input gives no configuration list of definitions. Theorem 15 is planned, not built, and is scored as if proved, as instructed.

The publisher page confirms the title, author, volume 359 (no. 4), pages 377–397 and year 2021. The fetched page showed the abstract and the bibliography (Kulaichev is reference [13]). The quoted passages on pp. 381 and 387 calling uniqueness 'toujours ouverte' could not be seen in the fetched text. This is a tooling limit, not a finding.

The record exists: Version 5, a preprint dated 20 Nov 2026, not peer reviewed. It states Theorems 14 and 15 as described. The record's title and the fourth condition carry the submitter's own names, which the blind input replaced. This matches the account. The description already discloses that the work is not peer reviewed.

Positive: it gives exact page citations for the published question, the degree bound and Rao's statement of unlimited solutions. It notes Pustynski's numerical, error-free uniqueness argument and the excentre second solution. It lists sources not read with reasons and gives the dates of the prior-formalization search. It makes no unsupported priority claim: the 'first proof' claim is limited to a condition the submitter introduced. It states plainly that no outside source asks for the golden product and that the 43/24 counts are not formalised. These are the grounds for the literature assessment.

Popular and journal sources link the Śrī Yantra to the golden ratio only loosely (Rao's height ratio near φ). No source found asks for a slope-product condition, which agrees with the account. This is not counted as evidence of novelty.

A credible area exists: the geometry of the Śrī Yantra and certified or computer-algebra solution of the constraint system (Huet, Kulaichev, Rao, Pustynski, Chiodo). What fails is the link between this particular theorem and that audience. The new condition can be read as chosen to produce a figure with the traditional counts, and this check found no evidence either way. The section-1 concern about 'definitions designed to manufacture the advertised conclusions' is not asserted. The failure is that paper-worthiness has not been affirmatively shown, not that the work is trivial: the planned proof (degree-160 elimination, an unbounded box, a degenerate-corner analysis) is substantial, but difficulty alone does not establish research interest under §1.

what_would_reach_higher: Put the property that makes this figure distinctive into the compared statements, for example a Lean statement that the unique figure's arrangement has exactly 43 triangles and 24 sandhis, or that this is the only figure in a well-defined family with the traditional counts.

Cite an independent source (traditional texts, Rao's or another author's specifications) showing that a condition equivalent to the golden slope product, or a property it secures, has been sought by others. Without that, the condition reads as the submitter's own choice.

Present this result alongside the answer to Kulaichev's own published question (Theorem 14). The comparison 'Kulaichev's condition gives 45 regions; this condition gives the traditional 43' is the part with specialist interest.

Give an argument that this fourth condition is canonical among the alternatives in #103 Table 3, for example a theorem classifying which slope-product conditions give the traditional counts. As it stands the account itself calls it one choice among several.
Get the motivating preprints (#103, #29, #44) peer reviewed, or cite independent reception, so the construction with solids rests on more than unreviewed self-citation.
